root_cause: Two planner passes combine. Pass 1 assigns a unit that stands partly in range of an objective to HOLD it and subtracts its WHOLE OC from the need: at s7454 r3 Beta (OC 9) had only 5 OC in range of obj_center vs 8 enemy OC (state enemy_weak), yet the centre's remaining need became 0, so Gamma's top candidate (centre, score 44.4) was skipped as 'already taken' and Beta's REMAIN_STATIONARY left the centre with the enemy. Pass 2 then greedily gave Gamma its next candidate with need left: a flip of obj_nml_1, held with OC 14 by the enemy, which Gamma (OC 9) cannot take even if the enemy never moves, with no other unit sent (score 15.0, threat_delta -16). Nothing in pass 2 compares a flip the plan cannot win against the enemy OC standing there NOW with a live fight the unit's own models could tip. A vs B records: in base A the enemy scored hold_central +3 per turn and per_objective 10/turn; in B (Gamma to the centre) P2 scored hold_new +3 and per_objective +8, and Centre Ground +3 in round 4; A only gained Engage on All Fronts +3 from Gamma's presence in the far quarter.
fix_summary: LONE-FLIP (FIX_LONE_FLIP=1, consts LONE_FLIP_MIN_GAIN=10, LONE_FLIP_MAX_TURNS=2) in _assign_units_to_objectives pass 2: when a capture candidate is a flip of an enemy-held objective (enemy_weak/enemy_strong) and ALL the OC the plan puts there (friendly OC in range, units en route, every unit the plan sends there at any arrival turn, this unit) is below the enemy OC on it now, the unit instead takes its best-scoring candidate (planner score >= flip + 10) at an objective where our models already stand in a live fight (held_threatened / contested / enemy_weak with friendly OC > 0 and friendly OC + this unit > enemy OC), reachable within 2 moves and passing TOO-LATE / RACE-SKIP / LONE-TRIP. It keeps the planner's own mode for that objective (here a Normal move, keeping shooting/charges). Not a veto: if no such live fight exists the flip stands, so the unit is never held back. Logs [LONE_FLIP] and a coordination_note on the unit's card. 0 = base behaviour exactly (the redirect returns {} first thing).

fires: [LONE_FLIP] fired 1 time in the finding replay (P2 round 3, Gamma obj_nml_1 -> obj_center) and 0 times in all 5 guardrail replays (both players, each played to the end of the next battle round), i.e. 1 decision changed in 6 replays (~0.2 per replay game). No SCRIPT ERRORs in any replay log.
risks: Rounds 3-5: the trigger is narrow (flip lost against the enemy OC already standing there AND a live fight with our models present scoring >= 10 more), so it rarely fires; when it does, the unit goes to an objective that pays every later round (primary hold/centre rules; Centre Ground, Burden of Trust-style hold cards) rather than being held back, so the round-2 FAR_TRIP failure mode (units idled away from far objectives) does not apply. Costs: (1) secondary cards that need units spread across quarters / enemy territory (Engage on All Fronts, Behind Enemy Lines, Outflank-type) can lose the presence the doomed flip gave — in the finding's base branch the lone flip earned Engage on All Fronts +3; the planner score's secondary terms are part of the 10-point margin but not explicitly checked. (2) In round 5 a lone flip can still deny/contest at the very end (equal OC does not flip, but killing holders can); LONE-FLIP only counts OC, not expected kills by melee, so a Custodes unit that would have charged and wiped part of the 14 OC is redirected. (3) The fix keeps the planner's mode (Normal move); the measured Advance alternative gained more (+21.5 vs +11.3 over 6 seeds), so the gain may be under-realised when the live fight needs the unit a turn sooner. (4) The deeper bug (pass 1 HOLD counting a partly-in-range holder's whole OC) is not fixed; LONE-FLIP only corrects its worst consequence. A full-game mirror benchmark is still needed.
